$comment: Volatile model facts for the /subscaler tier-composition toggle. The DURABLE contract is the tier vocabulary + the routing rubric in Superscalar.md §5.1; this file carries only the perishable part (which concrete models occupy which tier today, and what each vendor actually accepts as an effort value). Replace the data, keep the vocabulary. Every row is expected to carry a confirmedBy URL — an unverifiable claim belongs in caveats[], not in models[].
method: Six-axis live-source sweep (Anthropic / OpenAI / Google+xAI / open-weight / benchmarks / harness binding), each axis independently fact-checked by an adversarial pass instructed to refute; only vendor-page-confirmed ids and values were promoted here. Corrections applied included one fabricated model id, one shut-down model presented as current, and several mis-attributed benchmark sources. 2026-08-01 structural adjustment (not a data re-sweep): the T1.5 · Frontier Execution band was split out of T1 — the 2026-07-25 sweep recorded the 2x intra-T1 price spread ($10/$50 vs $5/$25) but the tier boundary absorbed it, and a temperament axis (think-to-action latency) surfaced in dogfood that the price rows do not carry. claude-opus-5 moved T1 → T1.5, and a per-account entitlement-check rule was added for invitation-gated models (claude-mythos-5). 2026-09-02 refresh — ANTHROPIC AXIS ONLY, triggered by the 2026-09-01 Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 launch (revisit rule (c): new flagship). Re-derived from the vendor models-overview, per-model overview, what's-new, migration-guide, pricing, model-deprecations and Claude Code model-config pages fetched the same day; two dated watchlist items were re-baselined (Sonnet 5 introductory pricing made permanent; Opus 4.1 retired 2026-08-05 with zero pins found in this estate). OpenAI, Google, xAI and open-weight rows were NOT re-swept in this pass and carry their 2026-07-25 / 2026-08-16 values; their watchlist items stand unverified. 2026-09-05 refresh, four axes, each run as two independent collectors plus one adversarial verifier that re-opened every cited URL and marked each field confirmed / unconfirmed / contradicted: Google Flash line (gemini-3.8-flash added, 3.7 Flash demoted to previous-generation), OpenAI (gpt-6-astra added; the entire gpt-5.6 family was found repriced on 2026-07-30 and is corrected here — neither collector looked at the sibling rows while standing on the pricing page), Anthropic Fable 5.1 delta (the Claude Code changelog for 2.1.257–2.1.261 was transcribed verbatim after both collectors mis-versioned three Fable-specific fixes when they summarized it), and harness binding (the Claude Code subagent model resolution order was found REVERSED since v2.1.251 — this registry carried the pre-reversal order through three refreshes because a version-range delta cannot see drift that entered before the range; Codex CLI 0.153.4 moved the bundled default to Astra). One standing claim was contradicted by the vendor page and re-baselined: the Google 2.5-family shutdown 2026-10-16 appears on no row of the deprecations page as of 2026-09-05. xAI and open-weight rows were NOT re-swept and remain on their 2026-07-25 / 2026-08-16 values. 2026-09-23 TARGETED refresh (not a full re-survey): four new rows (claude-opus-5-5, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna, grok-4.7) from vendor model/pricing/changelog pages read verbatim by one web-fetch lane per vendor (Anthropic, Claude Code, OpenAI+Codex, xAI), cross-checked against installed-harness primary sources (Claude Code 2.1.280 --help, codex-cli 0.156.0 client model catalog, grok CLI 1.0.40 model list); sibling rows annotated where the new models changed their standing. Google, DeepSeek, Zhipu, Moonshot and harnessProfile were NOT re-researched in this pass. 2026-09-29 TARGETED refresh: claude-sonnet-5-5 added from vendor pages read verbatim (per-model overview, what's new, models overview, pricing, effort, prompting guide, deprecations, launch page raw HTML, Claude Code model-config and changelog raw) by one lane plus an independent changelog/live-probe lane, then reconciled field by field (37 claims); Claude Code 2.1.284 accepted all five effort values live. planGating defaults that had drifted since v2.1.280 (Opus 5.5 became the default model) were corrected in the same pass. A separate communityRank block (see its own $comment) was added from an X sentiment sweep — it is a signal layer, not a sweep of models[] values. 2026-09-30 TARGETED refresh (OpenAI axis only): gpt-6.1-sol added from vendor pages read as .md (model page, pricing, changelog, GPT-6 guide, models index, model-selection, fast/ultrafast guides, deprecations), the Codex models and pricing docs (developers.openai.com/codex/models 308-redirects to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models), the openai.com launch post (direct fetch 403; read through the r.jina.ai reader), Codex release notes 0.157.0–0.159.2, and harness primaries (`codex debug models` live + --bundled on codex-cli 0.159.1, one live `codex exec` probe). Two collector lanes plus one adversarial verifier; 37 claims reconciled. gpt-6-sol re-annotated as superseded. Anthropic, Google, xAI and open-weight rows were NOT re-swept. 2026-10-08 FULL refresh (the scheduled revisit; benchmarks axis not run): five axes — Anthropic, OpenAI, Google+xAI, open-weight (DeepSeek, Z.ai, Moonshot, Alibaba Qwen, MiniMax, Xiaomi MiMo), harness binding (Claude Code, Codex CLI, grok CLI / Grok Build, Gemini CLI). Per axis one research lane ran TWO passes — (1) transcribe the vendor changelog / release notes / deprecations page since that axis's last refresh, (2) re-read every existing row against its own reference page, which is what caught drift outside any version window — then one adversarial verifier re-opened the sources as raw .md endpoints, curl, GitHub raw files, the HF API and the locally installed harness catalogs. Merged here: every research delta the verifier did not reject, with its corrections applied, plus the verifier's evidence-carrying «missed» items; rejected but plausible claims went to caveats. New rows: claude-haiku-5-5 (T4); deepseek-flash (REPLACES deepseek-v4-flash, now a retired alias served by V4.1 Flash); glm-5.3 (T2) and glm-5.3-flash (T3); qwen3.8-max (T2), qwen3.8-flash and qwen3.8-27b (T3); MiniMax-M3 (T3); mimo-v2.6-pro (T2) and mimo-v2.6-flash (T3) — all T-placements of the new open-weight rows are registry calls from price and positioning. New harnessBinding row: Grok Build CLI. Drift found outside any version window: claude-sonnet-5-5 cache read halved (2026-10-07); gemini-3.6-flash on the intro schedule since 2026-08-12..15 (stale here for eight weeks); deepseek-v4-pro repriced (peak/off-peak 2026-08-16, V4-Pro-0813); gemini-2.5-flash-lite still asserted a 2026-10-16 shutdown the 2026-09-05 pass had already disproved; Claude Code ultracode semantics changed in v2.1.284, inside the previous pass's own window. The WebFetch summarizer again mis-versioned every Claude Code changelog line it touched and silently dropped one release-note entry — the raw CHANGELOG.md and the .md doc endpoints were authoritative.

revisit.trigger: 2026-10-26 is the first revisit after the 2026-10-23 OpenAI shutdown cluster (o1 / o1-pro / o3-mini / o4-mini / ft-o4-mini, gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-4.1-nano, gpt-4o-2024-05-13 and their fine-tunes), so the post-cluster re-baseline the previous trigger scheduled runs on measured state rather than on notices. It also falls after three smaller dated events that need no registry change before they land but should be verified after: the gpt-5.5 Codex retirement (2026-10-14, API unaffected), the claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 retirement floor (2026-10-15 — no notice exists, and the 60-day rule means none issued now can retire it before 2026-12-07) and the MiMo v2.5 hard cutoff (2026-10-21, errors after). The next cluster is 2026-11-21 (gpt-5.6-sol promo floor) and 2026-11-30 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 retirement — the target of Claude Code's `sonnet` alias on Bedrock / Google Cloud / Foundry), so the follow-on revisit is ~2026-11-16. FORCE AN EARLIER REVISIT on: (a) any Fable 5 or Haiku 4.5 deprecation notice; (b) a new flagship from any vendor — Gemini Flash has been silent since 2026-09-02 against a vendor-stated three-in-six-weeks cadence, and no Grok 4.8 / Grok 5 / gpt-6.1 sibling / DeepSeek V4.1-Pro has shipped; (c) the first observed `The block is bound to a different conversation` 400 or a non-empty input_transformations in code here that assembles a `messages` array itself (re-scoped 2026-09-05; Claude Code ≤ 2.1.287 could itself drop earlier thinking — see watchlist); (d) any Claude Code release note touching model aliases (`fable` / `best` / `haiku`) — fired this pass (v2.1.293 `haiku` → Haiku 5.5); (e) the first observed silent effort clamp or model substitution in a scripted run — this pass recorded several new documented substitution surfaces (Claude Code 2.1.283–2.1.287, API sticky fallback routing); (f) OpenAI Decisions API GA or any change to its input-only pricing; (g) a DeepSeek V4.1-Pro launch, which by the vendor's own news post re-routes deepseek-v4-pro.
watchlist: Claude Fable 5 deprecation notice — none as of 2026-09-02 (Active, retirement not sooner than 2027-06-09), but it is now the superseded model of a live successor at the same price, exactly the position Opus 4.1 was in before its 2026-06-05 notice. Any pin to the literal id claude-fable-5 (not the `fable` alias) is the surface that would break; Claude Code ≥ v2.1.255 already rewrites such pins to the alias on first run. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations 2026-10-08: still NO notice (status table Active / N/A / Not sooner than June 9, 2027; newest history entry the 2026-09-30 Sonnet 4.5 notice). The model page now prints «Legacy.» and «Status | Active (legacy)» — Legacy is a defined lifecycle term now («may be deprecated in the future»), the same position Sonnet 4.5 was in before its notice.

Preserved-thinking enforcement widening, RE-SCOPED 2026-09-05: the vendor states «Claude Code, claude.ai, Claude Managed Agents, and the Claude Agent SDK keep that prefix intact for you», so the `The block is bound to a different conversation` 400 cannot originate from those harnesses — but «Future models are expected to enforce this check for all accounts». Live risk = EG-owned code that assembles a messages array itself (MCP servers, the board-observer turn spawner, scripted lanes). Probe those with thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior:"drop_block" (beta thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01), not the harness. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-1/whats-new-fable-5-1 2026-10-08: the harness itself was a source on older builds — Claude Code 2.1.287 «Fixed switching between Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 (`/model`, `opusplan`) rewriting earlier MCP tool announcements, which could drop earlier extended thinking» and 2.1.288 «Fixed resuming a conversation started on 2.1.286 or earlier dropping the model's earlier thinking». The «cannot originate from those harnesses» re-scope holds only on current builds; the local CLI here is 2.1.284.

Claude Code `fable` / `best` alias target — as of v2.1.255 `fable` = latest Fable (5.1) and `best` = latest Fable where available else `opus`, BUT v2.1.257 made the alias resolve DIFFERENTLY by provider surface: in Claude apps gateway sessions `fable`/`best` still mean Fable 5 «for now». Widen the check from «did the alias move» to «does the alias mean the same model on every surface this estate uses» — the gateway carve-out is explicitly temporary, so it will move again, and a `best` lane behind a gateway bills $1/MTok cache reads while the registry says $0.25. Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog · https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config 2026-10-08: unchanged — «the `fable` alias resolves to Fable 5.1, except in Claude apps gateway sessions, where `fable` and `best` resolve to Fable 5»; no 2.1.285–2.1.293 entry touches `fable` / `best` resolution. 2.1.287 made a /model Fable pick on a claude.ai login save the alias, so the saved default follows the newest Fable.

tiers.definition: The vendor's deepest-reasoning flagship, highest cost per token, thinking on by default and often not disableable. Characterized by sustained multi-hour autonomy, self-verification before acting, and the widest reasoning-effort ladder (including a top rung the cheaper tiers lack). Today: claude-fable-5-1 (claude-fable-5 stays as the legacy member), gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol, gemini-3.1-pro-preview, grok-4.5, kimi-k3; gated members: claude-mythos-5 (restricted access), gpt-5.5-pro (escalation-only).
tiers.selectionIntent: Select when the cost of a wrong answer exceeds the cost of the tokens: irreversible actions, ambiguous or under-specified inputs, architecture that later work will be built on, and adversarial review of another model's output. Do NOT select for volume — its per-token price is the tier's defining constraint, and vendor guidance is that a larger model can be cheaper per finished task only when the task is genuinely hard.

tiers.definition: The vendor's start-here flagship: frontier-class capability at roughly half T1 per-token price, positioned by the vendor itself as the default for complex agentic coding rather than for deepest deliberation. Split from T1 on temperament as much as price: it converts thinking into action sooner — speed on well-framed work, a slip risk on under-framed work. Today: claude-opus-5-5 (since 2026-09-22 — the vendor's «start with Opus 5.5» row; claude-opus-5 stays listed as the superseded legacy member). Vendors without a separate id here may span the band with a mode switch instead (gpt-5.6-sol reasoning.mode standard|pro) — such rows stay in T1 until measured. OpenAI's GPT-6 line is a 5x price split (Astra $10/$50 vs 6.1 Sol $2/$10) with no ~2x rung, so the band has no OpenAI member by construction; gpt-6.1-sol is the Codex default for complex agentic coding but stays T2 on price, API positioning and the vendor ladder (6.1 Sol xhigh < Astra low) until measured.
tiers.selectionIntent: Select for complex multi-step execution where judgment remains but the frame is already set: the daily-driver main loop, heavyweight implementation lanes, subagent leads. Always pair it with explicit verification gates (check-first, test gates) — the observed failure mode is premature action, and raising effort does not buy deliberation here. Escalate to T1 for architecture, ambiguous requirements, and adversarial review; drop to T2 once the spec is complete. Not a verification tier: adversarial review stays T1, cross-family.

tiers.definition: The workhorse: near-frontier coding capability at roughly a third to a half of T1 per-token cost, tuned for tool loops and multi-file edits, with a full effort ladder and a large (≥400K, usually ~1M) context window. Today: claude-sonnet-5-5 (since 2026-09-28; claude-sonnet-5 stays as the superseded legacy member) / claude-opus-4-8, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-6.1-sol (gpt-6-sol stays as the superseded legacy member), gemini-3.8-flash (3.7 / 3.6 / 3.5 Flash stay as previous-generation and legacy members), grok-4.3, glm-5.3 (glm-5.2 stays as the superseded member), deepseek-v4-pro, qwen3.8-max, mimo-v2.6-pro.
tiers.selectionIntent: The default tier for the main coding loop once the decision is already made and the spec is written. Select whenever the work is 'do the thing correctly' rather than 'decide what the thing is'. This is where a maintainer should spend most tokens; escalation to T1 should be the exception you can name a reason for.

tiers.definition: Cheap-but-competent models the vendor itself markets for subagents and fan-out — real code edits and real tool use, but a smaller window or a shallower reasoning ceiling than T2. Typically 5-15x cheaper on output than T1. Today: gpt-6-luna, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.4-mini, grok-build-0.1, deepseek-flash (V4.1 Flash; deepseek-v4-flash is a retired alias of it), glm-5.3-flash, qwen3.8-flash, qwen3.8-27b, MiniMax-M3, mimo-v2.6-flash.
tiers.selectionIntent: Select for wide parallel lanes where the unit of work is small, independently verifiable, and cheap to redo: read-heavy scans, large-file review, per-file mechanical edits, test scaffolding. The economic point of this tier is that a failed lane is cheap to re-run, so buy width instead of depth.

tiers.definition: The cheapest always-on tier: sub-$1 input, minimal or off-by-default thinking, lowest latency floor. Marketed for classification, extraction, routing and watch loops rather than authoring. Often has NO effort parameter at all (the legacy claude-haiku-4-5) or defaults to none/minimal (gpt-5.4-nano, gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-2.5-flash-lite) — but since 2026-10-07 the current Anthropic member, claude-haiku-5-5, HAS a full effort ladder (default medium) and adaptive thinking on by default (always on in Claude Code), and it runs refusal classifiers with no server-side fallback, so «minimal thinking» and «never refuses a watch event» are no longer tier-wide traits. Today: claude-haiku-5-5 (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 stays as the legacy member, floor 2026-10-15, no deprecation notice), gpt-5.4-nano (deprecated 2026-10-01, removed 2027-04-01 → gpt-6-luna), gemini-3.5-flash-lite / gemini-3.1-flash-lite / gemini-2.5-flash-lite (2.5: access limited to existing users since 2026-09-18).
tiers.selectionIntent: Select for anything that must run continuously and mostly return 'nothing to do': inbox/board polling, event classification, triage routing, digest extraction. Budget it as a fixed monthly cost, not per-task. Never let this tier author code or make a routing decision that is expensive to reverse — its job is to decide whether to wake a higher tier.

aliases: claude-fable-5-1 (the dateless id is its own pinned snapshot; the alias row repeats it)
anthropic.claude-fable-5-1 (Amazon Bedrock)

Claude Code: `fable` → «the latest Fable model for your hardest and longest-running tasks»; `best` → «the latest Fable model where it's available to you, otherwise the same model as `opus`» (v2.1.255+) — EXCEPT in Claude apps gateway sessions, where v2.1.257 changed `fable` and `best` to keep resolving to Fable 5 «for now, since gateways not yet configured for Fable 5.1 reject it»; there, pick Fable 5.1 explicitly in `/model`. Don't read a `best`/`fable` lane as «running 5.1» without checking the session's provider — the alias silently means a different model, and a different cache-read price, behind a gateway.
models.contextWindow: 1M input (default AND maximum, standard per-token price across the whole window) / 128k max output. NOT on the vendor's Batch-API output-300k list (that list names Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 4.6 only). Tokenizer = Fable 5 = the Opus 4.7 line (~30% more tokens than pre-4.7 models for the same text). Claude Code v2.1.260 changed auto-compact for 1M-context models so «Opus and Fable sessions now compact shortly before the 1M-token limit», and stopped recovery compaction on very large contexts timing out at 10 minutes; before that a 1M lane compacted against the older threshold. Same release fixed `model: fable` subagents ignoring the `[1m]` tag on an `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL` pin and «silently running with a 200K context window» — on ≤2.1.259 a `[1m]`-pinned fan-out lane is not the window it claims to be, and nothing in the transcript says so. Don't infer the effective window from the pin; it is a silent downgrade.
models.pricingPerMTok: $10 input / $50 output — same as Fable 5. Cache write $12.50 (5m) / $20 (1h). Cache read $0.25 = 0.025× base (a quarter of Fable 5's $1; every other Claude model is 0.1×). Batch $5 / $25. inference_geo:"us" ×1.1 on all categories. Priority Tier: NOT supported (Fable 5 is). Fast mode: not offered (Opus 5 / 4.8 only). Vendor's own aggregate framing (2026-09-01 announcement): «Fable 5.1 will cost an estimated 25% less than Fable 5 for typical workloads, wherever usage is billed by token», «For highly agentic work, the savings will often be much larger—up to approximately 45%», «Cache reads now cost 75% less, or $0.25 per million tokens». Every dollar of that saving lives in cache reads alone — base input, output, cache writes and batch are byte-identical to Fable 5 — so a lane that misses the cache saves exactly nothing and the 25%/45% figures do not apply to it. Two consequences worth acting on: (a) the vendor now advises compacting LATER, not earlier — «Because cache reads are now cheaper, compacting early to save cost may no longer be the right cost-intelligence tradeoff on Claude Fable 5.1, so experiment with later compaction points»; (b) Claude Code BEFORE v2.1.260 did not cache the context attached after tool results on Fable 5.1 and re-sent it as uncached input on every tool-call turn — an agentic session on v2.1.255–2.1.259 (this workspace's recorded v2.1.258 included) pays $10/MTok where it should pay $0.25. Don't benchmark Fable 5.1 cost on a pre-2.1.260 harness; upgrade first, then measure.
models.effort: output_config.effort = low | medium | high (default) | xhigh | max. Thinking ALWAYS ON — thinking:{type:"disabled"} and {type:"enabled",budget_tokens:N} both 400; non-default temperature/top_p/top_k 400; assistant prefill 400. Per-message effort change WITHOUT cache invalidation: beta header mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01, an effort-only {role:"system", content:[], output_config:{effort}} entry in messages (also Mythos 5.1 and Opus 5; Claude API). Vendor calibration: «At medium, results roughly match Claude Fable 5 at lower cost»; «At low, Claude Fable 5.1 is often competitive with Claude Opus and Claude Sonnet models on cost per task while scoring higher» — re-run the effort sweep even if one exists for Fable 5 (level names do not carry across models). Effort-specific shifts: at low it calls search/retrieval less and answers from memory more; at xhigh/max it may draft a long deliverable in thinking and again in the reply (set max_tokens for thinking+reply, or stay at high). Claude Code exposes the same five levels; `ultracode` = xhigh + workflow orchestration (v2.1.203+). Claude Code specifics, re-measured 2026-09-05. Fable 5.1 has NO cross-session default-effort hold: the vendor names the hold for Fable 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 and then states «Opus 5 and Fable 5.1 have no such hold», so a settings-resolved level applies from the first run and the `--effort`-at-launch workaround is unnecessary here. `/effort s` (v2.1.257+) scopes a change to the current session only, matching `/model`. Changing effort mid-session stopped invalidating the prompt cache on Fable 5.1 in v2.1.260 — the harness-side expression of the mid-conversation-output-config beta; on ≤2.1.259 each effort change still costs a full uncached re-read, so a per-step effort ladder is a pessimization there. `ultracode` is NOT a sixth effort value: the persisted `effortLevel` setting and `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` do not accept it, and «When `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` is set to a level other than `xhigh`, requests run at that level and ultracode's workflow orchestration stays inactive» — an env pin therefore disables orchestration SILENTLY even when a lane asks for ultracode. Reach it only via `/effort ultracode`, `--effort ultracode`, `"ultracode": true` in a settings file or `--settings` or an Agent SDK control request (`applyFlagSettings({effortLevel:"ultracode"})`), or the `/model` picker's effort slider. Don't set ultracode through env and don't assume a scripted lane got it.
models.notes: Released 2026-09-01. Vendor: «For demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work» — «or when your evals on Claude Opus 5 at higher effort still fall short»; the vendor's start-here model was Opus 5 at launch (Opus 5.5 since 2026-09-22). Latency «Slower»; single requests can run many minutes. Reliable knowledge cutoff Jun 2026 (training cutoff Jun 2026). Status Active (latest); retirement not sooner than 2027-09-01. Successor to Fable 5 in the same tier at the same per-token price; migration is «mostly drop-in» with THREE BREAKING CHANGES: ① forced tool use — tool_choice {type:"any"} / {type:"tool"} return 400 «tool_choice: type "tool" and "any" are not supported for this model.» (also on Batches and count_tokens) → keep auto + name the tool in the prompt, strict:true for schema-valid args, or structured outputs; ② thinking blocks are bound to the producing model — Fable 5.1 reads earlier models' blocks, no earlier model reads 5.1's; a router/fallback that moves the conversation off 5.1 drops them silently and unbilled (beta thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01 reports drops in input_transformations); ③ editing anything before a 5.1 thinking block (system, tools, an earlier message, injected-then-removed reminders, a URL serving different bytes) invalidates every later block → 400 «The block is bound to a different conversation» — ENFORCED for accounts created on/after 2026-08-31, record-only for older accounts unless thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior is set; safe operations: dropping a leading run of thinking blocks, server-side compaction/context editing, moving cache_control, changing effort. Mythos 5.1 does NOT run check ③. FIVE ADDITIVE: per-message effort (see effort); turn-scoped system messages clear_at:"next_user_message" (beta mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21 — the vendor's replacement for inject-and-delete reminders; cleared copies cost 0 input tokens and must stay in the array byte-for-byte); thinking.display:"updates" (beta thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18) returns between-tool-call progress notes as text while reasoning stays hidden (default display is still "omitted" = empty blocks = silent-looking agent); cache reads at $0.25; content provenance — every text output carries Anthropic's statistical watermark on every platform, image/video files via Files API carry signed C2PA credentials (no tokens added, no change to requests). Refusals: same stop_details categories as Fable 5 («fewer false positives than Claude Fable 5's did at launch, and finding vulnerabilities in source code is permitted»); fallbacks:"default" (beta) retries a declined request on the category's recommended model — permitted targets Opus 4.8 and Opus 5 (Claude Code: cybersecurity → Opus 4.8, biology → Opus 5; togglable via switchModelsOnFlag); a refusal before any output is not billed and fallback credit refunds the cache-switch cost (STALE since 2026-09-24 for bio / frontier_llm / reasoning_extraction — see the 2026-10-08 note). Data: 30-day retention required, designated Covered Model, no ZDR unless expressly authorized (a request from a ZDR org/workspace returns 400 invalid_request_error). Platforms: Claude API, Amazon Bedrock (anthropic.claude-fable-5-1), Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry — note Opus 5 shows «—» for Claude Platform on AWS while 5.1 is listed. BEHAVIOR SHIFTS vs Fable 5 (vendor-documented, each with a prompt fix — see harnessProfile): parallel tool calling more variable when the next reads are only implied by a coding/computer-use loop; fewer user-facing progress updates, more so at high effort; denser prose in places; less bold/headers/lists in chat (anti-formatting rules written for older models now suppress needed structure); unmarked quotations in summaries; whole-file rewrites for small edits. Claude Code: reach via /model fable (or `best`), never the account default on any plan or provider, minimum Claude Code v2.1.255, may bill usage credits depending on plan/seat («Requires usage credits» in the picker; interactive sessions ask consent), hidden under ZDR; settings pinned to `claude-fable-5` are auto-rewritten to the `fable` alias on first run of v2.1.255+. Vendor pages used: overview · what's-new · migration guide · pricing · model-deprecations · Claude Code model-config (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-1/whats-new-fable-5-1 · https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-1/migration-guide · https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config). 2026-09-05 delta pass. PROMPTING: the vendor ships a dedicated page, «Prompting Claude Fable 5.1» (16 sections), and it carries fixes the model page does not list: «Finish the whole task» (the model stops to ask «Shall I apply this?» or narrates the next step instead of doing it; the vendor's two-block system prompt opens «You are operating autonomously. The user is not watching in real time and cannot answer questions mid-task» and that sentence «carries much of the effect»), «Keep changes and tests to what the task asks for» (unrequested adjacent fixes and committed test files «drop substantially with no measurable change in task success»), «Tell the model what to preserve in compaction summaries» (a six-item preservation list; server-side compaction already does this, so it is a client-compaction fix only), «Let the lead agent keep working while subagents run» (a start-subagent tool that returns immediately + results delivered as a later user message + a separate wait tool «lowers average time to completion at similar quality, token usage, and cost»), «Give vision work tools to crop and zoom», «Consider all effort levels», and «Reduce safeguard false positives» with three named triggers — compile-check phrasing (ask «Are there any bugs in this program?», not «Does this program compile without errors?»), lesser-known programming languages (give the model the language's documentation), and base64-encoded data in tool output (remove it). DON'T paste those prompt blocks into a harness that already says the same thing — «Finish the whole task» duplicates this workspace's autonomy rule and «Keep changes to what the task asks for» duplicates its scope rule; doubling a system prompt buys nothing and lengthens the cached prefix. PRESERVED-THINKING SCOPE NARROWED: the vendor states «Claude Code, claude.ai, Claude Managed Agents, and the Claude Agent SDK keep that prefix intact for you», so breaking change ③ is a risk for code that builds the `messages` array itself, NOT for lanes running inside those harnesses — don't spend a probe cycle proving the harness safe. Sharpening: «Removing a thinking block from anywhere other than the start of the run invalidates every thinking block after it.» SAFEGUARDS, QUANTIFIED (announcement page, not the docs): «In cybersecurity, our newest safeguards block 60% fewer false positives than before», «Claude Code users can expect an average of around 60% fewer interventions per session from our cyber safeguards», and biology safeguards «fire 85% less often for benign requests related to elementary biology and medical questions» — read that last one carefully: it is scoped to «Fable 5.1 and Fable 5», so it is a safeguard-generation improvement, not a 5.1-over-5 differentiator. A system card («Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1») is linked from the announcement; not read this pass, publication date unverified. RE-VERIFIED UNCHANGED 2026-09-05: the id `claude-fable-5-1`; every price including the 0.025× cache-read multiplier (now also stated on the general pricing page, so it is vendor-canonical rather than one page's artifact); the four platforms with their exact ids; Active with «Not sooner than September 1, 2027»; and no new Anthropic deprecation notice of any kind — the newest entry in the deprecation history is still 2026-06-05 (Opus 4.1). Claude Code's highest published version on 2026-09-05 is v2.1.261; there is no 2.1.262+. In-house trust-cost measurement, including the comparison with Fable 5 by effort: see inHouse. 2026-10-08 RE-CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: id, $10/$50, cache write $12.50/$20, cache read $0.25 (0.025x), batch $5/$25, 1M/128K, thinking adaptive and always on, default effort high, all five levels, per-message effort on the Claude API / Google Cloud / Bedrock, Active (latest), retirement not sooner than 2027-09-01, five platforms; the vendor start-here pointer is Opus 5.5. REFUSAL BILLING CHANGED 2026-09-24: «We're resuming billing for refusals that arrive before any output when `stop_details.category` is "bio", "frontier_llm", or "reasoning_extraction" … Refusals billed under this change are charged like any other request, at the rates of the model that ran it.» Cyber, general_harms and null-category refusals before output stay free — so on this row a biology refusal before output is now a paid request. CLAUDE CODE: `fable` → Fable 5.1 except in Claude apps gateway sessions, where `fable` and `best` still resolve to Fable 5 (unchanged); 2.1.287 «Fixed picking Fable in `/model` on a claude.ai login saving the current version's id, so your saved default now follows the newest Fable»; 2.1.287 made Opus 4.7+ and Fable default to a 1M window on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and the Claude apps gateway (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1` keeps 200K); 2.1.286 made the fallback notice say when a fallback dropped the window from 1M to 200K. Requires Claude Code ≥ v2.1.257 for 5.1 (vendor page).

THE DEFAULT DROPPED A RUNG: «A request that omits `effort` runs at `medium`; on Claude Opus 5 it ran at `high`.» Vendor: «Opus 5.5 at medium matches or exceeds Opus 5 at high on coding and knowledge-work evaluations, and on several coding evaluations low comes close to it», but also «At a given level, Claude Opus 5.5 tends to think more per turn than Claude Opus 5, especially at xhigh and max» — so a lane copied from Opus 5 at the same effort name gets LONGER turns, not the same ones. «Reserve xhigh and max for work where you've measured a quality gain.» Thinking is adaptive and ALWAYS ON (thinking disabled or enabled+budget_tokens → 400). Claude Code 2.1.280: an effort saved before /effort became per-model no longer applies to newly released models such as Opus 5.5 — they start at their default. Claude Code default CONFIRMED 2026-10-08 verbatim (model-config.md): «`high` on every model that supports effort, except that Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5 default to `medium`…» — the same as the API. models.notes: Released 2026-09-22 («Latest.»), retirement not sooner than 2027-09-22; the first model of the Claude 5.5 family. Positioning moved the start-here pointer: «If you're unsure which model to use, start with Claude Opus 5.5 for most workloads» — with Fable 5.1 reserved «for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work, or when your evals on Claude Opus 5.5 at higher effort still fall short». Vendor claim: «performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5», output >30% faster than Opus 5, better sustained multi-hour autonomous runs «with parallel subagents and little oversight», and the strongest indirect-prompt-injection resistance of any Opus. FIRST Opus launched with Fable-class safeguards (cyber, biology, distillation) that «fall back to another model transparently» — a lane can be silently served by a different model on those topics (2026-10-08: the refusals page now states fallbacks are VISIBLE — see below). BREAKING vs Opus 5 (four): thinking cannot be disabled; forced tool use (`tool_choice` any/tool) returns 400 — «say in the prompt when the tool applies» or use strict tools/structured outputs; thinking blocks are bound to model+conversation (Opus 5.5 reads Opus 5-and-earlier blocks but not Fable/Mythos ones; a changed prefix before a replayed block is a 400 by default for accounts created on or after 2026-08-31, opt-in drop via thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01); `computer_20251124` rejected on the Claude API and Google Cloud (still fine on Bedrock). Non-failing but loud: text between tool calls arrives in EMPTY thinking blocks at the default display — a harness that streamed it as progress goes quiet until it sets display:"updates" (thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18). Unattended-loop foot-gun: «some of those updates end the turn with text rather than a tool call (stop_reason: "end_turn")» — a loop that treats end_turn as task end stops early. models.notes: Released 2026-09-02, GA on day one. Vendor tagline: "Our most intelligent Flash model, engineered for long-horizon software engineering, autonomous agents, and complex enterprise workflows"; the models index badges it "New Stable" and demotes BOTH 3.7 and 3.6 Flash to "Our previous-generation Flash model" in the same breath. Knowledge cutoff March 2026, with some domains limited to January 2025 (model card). Displaces gemini-3.7-flash as Google's T2 pick on vendor framing alone — the price, window, modalities and thinking ladder are byte-identical, so the switch is free and staying on 3.7 needs a measured reason, not the reverse. DO NOT budget it as a drop-in token-cost equal despite the identical rate card: the model card warns "the model might use more tokens to maximize performance, especially at higher effort levels", which is the same cost-per-finished-task trap the 3.5-vs-3.6 Flash rows already carry — measure output tokens on your own workload before assuming parity. DO NOT plan a Gemini CLI lane on this id (SUPERSEDED 2026-10-08 — now allowlisted, see below): it was ABSENT from VALID_GEMINI_MODELS as of 2026-09-05 (checked live), as are 3.7 AND 3.6 — three consecutive releases missing, so the CLI allowlist lag is now structural, not a gap; that harness still hardcodes DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL = gemini-2.5-pro and DEFAULT_GEMINI_FLASH_MODEL = gemini-2.5-flash. This model was API / AI Studio / Vertex / Antigravity only at that time. Vendor cadence, in its own words: "Our third Flash release in only six weeks" (3.6 on 2026-07-21 → 3.7 on 2026-08-13 → 3.8 on 2026-09-02) — treat any Gemini Flash row here as perishable within three weeks. No deprecation was triggered for 3.7 / 3.6 / 3.5 Flash: the deprecations page lists all three, and 3.8 itself, as "No shutdown date announced". A gated sibling shipped the same day — Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, restricted to "a set of trusted defenders via the Fairwind Program" (government authorities, critical-infrastructure operators, software maintainers); NO API id is published on any reachable vendor page, so DO NOT guess gemini-3.8-flash-cyber, and treat program membership the way the registry treats claude-mythos-5: recognition is not entitlement. Benchmark caution: the launch post names DeepSWE v1.1, Vals Finance Agent V2, Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark, CyberGym, CWE-Bench and Gray Swan IPI, but the only figures I could read verbatim were HLE-Verified 54.9%, an internal vulnerability benchmark at "70%+ success rate" and CWE-Bench 47.2% pass@1 — every head-to-head delta against 3.7 Flash in circulation is unverified here, so do not quote one. Vertex AI endpoint string, launch stage and region list are UNCONFIRMED: cloud.google.com 301s to docs.cloud.google.com and that page returned navigation only. 2026-10-08 RE-CONFIRMED: 1,048,576/65,536; thinking low|medium (default, «On (medium)»)|high, «minimal is not supported and returns an error»; intro $0.75/$3.75 (cache $0.075, storage $0.50) through 2026-12-31 then $1.50/$7.50 ($0.15, $1.00); batch/flex $0.375/$1.875; priority $1.35/$6.75 → $2.70/$13.50 and priority cache $0.135 → $0.27 (not recorded before); computer use preview; model page last updated 2026-09-02; «No shutdown date announced»; models-index badge «New Stable». GEMINI CLI: now allowlisted — `LATEST_GEMINI_FLASH_MODEL = 'gemini-3.8-flash'` (commit «Feat/gemini 3.8 flash 3.5 flash lite (#29443)», 2026-09-22; listed in the v0.62.0 release notes 2026-09-29; present in the v0.63.0 tag file 2026-10-06). The CLI REWRITES 'gemini-3.5-flash', 'gemini-3-flash', 'flash' and the preview id to it when the account has the latest-Flash GA flag, so only the explicit id is pin-stable. LATEST-MODEL GUIDE (docs/latest-model, the page the changelog links): «Gemini 3.8 Flash can use more tokens on longer running and complex tasks, by design. … For everyday tasks, you can lower the reasoning effort to reduce token consumption. Alternatively, Gemini 3.7 Flash remains fully supported.»; its migration checklist adds removing prefilled model turns, standardizing on server-side previous_interaction_id, and FunctionResponse objects carrying call_id and name on generateContent; «the Antigravity agent, now uses Gemini 3.8 Flash» (managed agents and the Antigravity SDK default). taskShapeRouting.why: Fable 5's documented strength (carried into Fable 5.1, whose gains the vendor says are «largest at the higher settings») is that it "investigates before acting" and self-verifies, which is precisely what an under-specified request needs; a cheaper tier will confidently resolve the ambiguity the wrong way and the error surfaces only after the code is written.

taskShapeRouting.taskShape: Complex multi-step execution with residual judgment (daily-driver main loop, heavyweight implementation lanes)
taskShapeRouting.effort: high (the default); do not raise effort to buy deliberation — pair with verification gates (check-first, test gates) instead (2026-10-08: «the default» is medium on claude-opus-5-5 — the current T1.5 member — on both the Claude API and Claude Code, and high only on the legacy claude-opus-5.)
taskShapeRouting.why: The vendor positions claude-opus-5 as the start-here model for complex agentic coding at half T1 price; dogfood observation (2026-08-01) adds the boundary — it acts sooner than T1, so this band buys frontier capability for execution while decisions (architecture, ambiguity) and adversarial review stay on T1 and spec-complete work drops to T2. (2026-10-08: the vendor's start-here row has been claude-opus-5-5 since 2026-09-22 — «If you're unsure which model to use, start with Claude Opus 5.5 for most workloads».)

taskShapeRouting.effort: medium first on Sonnet 5.5, high for harder/longer work — the vendor start point for agentic coding is «start with `medium` for well-specified tasks and move to `high` for harder or longer ones». Levels are recalibrated vs Sonnet 5 («Run a fresh effort sweep … rather than carrying over the setting you used on Claude Sonnet 5»), so there is no rung-equivalence line for 5.5. Harness caveat: Claude Code and the Claude apps default Sonnet 5.5 to medium while the Claude API defaults to high. (On the superseded Sonnet 5: medium is «Comparable to Claude Sonnet 4.6 at high effort».)
taskShapeRouting.why: Vendor guidance is to "Pick a smaller model when the work is routine. For example, edits you can describe precisely" — once the decision is made the remaining risk is execution fidelity, which T2 buys at a third to a half the per-token cost.

Vendor effort table puts low at "short, scoped, latency-sensitive tasks that are not intelligence-sensitive" and warns that max "is prone to overthinking" on structured-output work — a rote rename is exactly the shape where extra reasoning invents unrequested changes.

taskShapeRouting.effort: medium, raised to high when tests must infer intent rather than mirror a spec
taskShapeRouting.why: Test bodies are mostly mechanical once the contract is fixed, but choosing WHICH cases matter is a judgement step; medium keeps cost down while leaving enough reasoning to enumerate edge cases, and you raise effort only on the observed failure of missing them.

OpenAI's Codex subagent doc names this shape verbatim for its execution tier — "agents that favor speed and efficiency over depth, such as exploration, read-heavy scans, large-file review" — and Anthropic notes lower effort makes FEWER tool calls, which is the dominant cost term in a search lane.

taskShapeRouting.effort: low; none or minimal where the vendor offers it (gpt-5.4-nano defaults to none, gemini-3.5-flash-lite to minimal)
taskShapeRouting.why: Anthropic's effort docs list "simple classification tasks, quick lookups, or high-volume use cases" as the canonical low-effort case; reasoning adds cost without changing a well-specified extraction, and the cheap tiers already default to the right rung.

taskShapeRouting.effort: medium — the binding constraint is window and per-token price, not reasoning depth
taskShapeRouting.why: Every current T2 carries ~1M context, but the cost cliffs sit at different thresholds — >272K doubles input on the GPT-5.6 family, ≥200k doubles it on all Grok models and on gemini-3.1-pro-preview — so the routing decision here is which cliff you can stay under, and deepseek-v4-pro's $0.003625 cache-hit rate is the cheapest way to re-read the same corpus. (2026-10-08: deepseek-v4-pro's cache hit is now $0.022 off-peak / $0.044 peak after its 2026-08 repricing; the lowest re-read rate among 1M-context T2 rows is now mimo-v2.6-pro's $0.0036 overseas cache hit, and DeepSeek peak hours double every cell.)

taskShapeRouting.effort: minimal or none; low only when the watcher must classify intent rather than match a pattern
taskShapeRouting.why: Google's changelog calls gemini-3.5-flash-lite "a low-latency, highly cost-effective subagent option" and ships it with thinking_level defaulting to "minimal" — the vendor has already tuned this tier for the wake-or-ignore loop, and the observer's only real decision is whether to escalate. (2026-10-08: OpenAI shipped a purpose-built surface for exactly this decision — the Decisions API beta on gpt-6-luna, input-only at $0.10/MTok — unmeasured here; and claude-haiku-5-5, the new Anthropic T4, refuses cyber / bio-flagged events with no fallback, which a watcher must handle.)

taskShapeRouting.effort: xhigh — "Deeper reasoning at higher token spend"
taskShapeRouting.why: Verification is the one shape where paying T1 rates on a small input is clearly worth it, because a missed defect is discovered downstream at far higher cost; running the verifier on the same model that authored the code correlates the blind spots, so cross-vendor separation is the point, not a nicety.

effortGuidance: Default first, escalate on evidence — not on principle. Anthropic's own Claude Code guidance is "For most tasks you should use the model's default effort level", and to "Pick a higher effort level if Claude got it wrong by skipping a file, not running the tests, or not double-checking its work." Escalation should be traceable to an observed failure mode, not to the importance of the task.

NON-MONOTONICITY IS VENDOR-DOCUMENTED, not folklore. Claude Code's effort table says of max: "Can improve performance on demanding tasks but may show diminishing returns and is prone to overthinking. Test before adopting broadly." The API docs are blunter for the Opus 4.7/4.8 line: "On most workloads max adds significant cost for relatively small quality gains, and on some structured-output or less intelligence-sensitive tasks it can lead to overthinking." A blanket always-max policy is therefore a documented anti-pattern, not merely expensive.

Effort level names are NOT comparable across models: "The effort scale is calibrated per model, so the same level name does not represent the same underlying value across models." Any harness that stores one global effort setting and applies it to whatever model is active is storing a meaningless number — bind effort per model, as Claude Code does with per-subagent and per-skill `effort` frontmatter.

Carried-over settings are actively harmful after a model change. Anthropic on Opus 5: "If you carried effort settings over from an earlier model, run a fresh effort sweep on your evals rather than reusing them." This bites hardest in Claude Code, where Fable 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 HOLD their default effort until you make an explicit choice, but Opus 5 has no such hold — a level you set for another model silently carries over.

Step DOWN the ladder before stepping across tiers. Vendor guidance for Fable 5: "Lower effort settings on Claude Fable 5 still perform well and often exceed xhigh performance on prior models." And for Sonnet 5, medium is "Comparable to Claude Sonnet 4.6 at high effort." A generation bump usually means the cheap rung of the new model beats the expensive rung of the old one — check that before downgrading tier. 2026-09-28, Sonnet 5.5: «On several benchmarks, Sonnet 5.5 at Low or Medium effort beats Sonnet 5's best score for about a tenth of the cost per task» (vendor-stated) — the same generation-bump pattern, now inside T2. But its levels are recalibrated («a level doesn't produce the same amount of thinking as the same level on Claude Sonnet 5»), so step-down decisions need a fresh sweep, not a carried-over number; and one model now has two defaults (Claude API high, Claude Code/apps medium).

Low effort is the intended subagent setting, and it changes tool behavior, not just prose. The effort docs list low's typical use as "Simpler tasks that need the best speed and lowest costs, such as subagents", and state that lower effort makes the model "Combine multiple operations into fewer tool calls" and "Make fewer tool calls". In a search or exploration lane, tool-call count is the dominant cost term, so low effort saves more than the token delta suggests.

Effort is a behavioral signal, not a token budget: "At lower effort levels, Claude will still think on sufficiently difficult problems, but it will think less than it would at higher effort levels for the same problem." You cannot use effort as a hard cost cap — pair it with max_tokens, and conversely at xhigh/max the docs tell you to set a LARGE max_tokens ("Starting at 64k tokens") or the model runs out of room mid-thought.

Effort is a caching decision as much as a quality decision: "Changing the effort value between requests invalidates prompt caching, so vary effort across workloads rather than within a conversation that relies on cache hits." For a long resident session, pick one level at session start and hold it; dynamic per-turn effort tuning can cost more than it saves.

On Opus 5, do not use effort to control verbosity — "changing effort does not reliably shorten responses, so prompt for length instead." Harnesses that lowered effort to cut output size on older models will see the cost saving without the brevity, and Opus 5 is separately reported to narrate more than 4.8 by default.

Know the two default-effort exceptions before you trust a default. In Claude Code "The default effort is high on every model that supports effort, except Opus 4.7, which defaults to xhigh." On the OpenAI side the exception runs the other way: gpt-5.4-mini and gpt-5.4-nano default reasoning.effort to `none`, so omitting the parameter gives you a non-reasoning model on a code-editing lane. 2026-10-08: the Claude Code sentence now has a medium group — «`high` on every model that supports effort, except that Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5 default to `medium`, Opus 4.7 defaults to `xhigh`…» — so the CURRENT Anthropic lineup mostly defaults to medium. On the OpenAI side, gpt-5.4-nano's `none` default is the trap when moving a lane to its named replacement gpt-6-luna (default `medium`).

Anthropic's cheap tier has NO effort knob at all: claude-haiku-4-5 rejects the effort parameter and has no adaptive thinking. That asymmetry is a routing constraint, not a detail — if your resident-observer lane needs a dial, Google's Flash-Lite line (minimal/low/medium/high) or gpt-5.4-nano gives you one and Haiku does not. 2026-10-08: no longer true of Anthropic's CURRENT cheap tier — claude-haiku-5-5 «is the first Haiku model with effort levels» (low…max, default medium; adaptive thinking on by default, always on in Claude Code). The no-knob statement now describes only the legacy claude-haiku-4-5-20251001.

On Google, effort control is now the ONLY supported determinism knob: the 2026-07-21 changelog deprecated temperature, top_p and top_k in the Gemini API. Any harness pinning temperature for reproducible output must migrate to thinking_level.

xAI has no low end of the ladder: for grok-4.5 the values are low, medium, high (default high) and "Reasoning cannot be disabled" — there is no none/minimal rung, so xAI cannot serve a true resident-observer lane on effort alone. Separately, on grok-4.20-multi-agent, effort selects AGENT COUNT (4 or 16) rather than reasoning depth, which makes xhigh there a 16x token multiplier rather than a deeper single pass. UPDATE 2026-08-16: grok-4.6 adds "xhigh" ABOVE high (default still high) — the ladder grew at the top, and the bottom is still missing: there is no none/minimal anywhere in xAI's lineup, so T3/T4-style minimal-effort lanes still cannot be expressed on xAI models. 2026-10-08: grok-4.3's page now states `none` («Supports none (no reasoning at all), low, medium, and high»; default low) — xAI DOES have a none rung, on grok-4.3 only; 4.5 / 4.6 / 4.7 still say «Reasoning cannot be disabled».

`ultracode` and `ultrathink` are not effort levels and should not be modelled as such. Ultracode "is a Claude Code setting rather than a model effort level: it sends xhigh to the model and additionally has Claude orchestrate dynamic workflows", is session-only, and is rejected by both the persisted effortLevel setting and CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL. Ultrathink "adds an in-context instruction" and "The effort level sent to the API is unchanged" — so it costs nothing at the API-parameter layer and changes nothing there either. 2026-10-08: since Claude Code 2.1.284 ultracode «no longer forces xhigh effort and stays on at any effort level», and it CAN now be persisted (`"ultracode": true` settings key); only `--effort ultracode` / SDK effortLevel 'ultracode' also set xhigh.

A T1 main inherits into every fan-out lane by default, and on Fable 5.1 that default is the expensive failure mode. Claude Code (v2.1.251+) resolves a subagent's model as per-invocation `model` → frontmatter `model` → CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL (a default, not a pin) → the main conversation's model, and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` (v2.1.257+) overrides all of them — including bindings a guard just approved, which is why the reference guard reads that variable, and a Workflow lane that omits opts.model does the same — so with Fable 5.1 as main, an unbound research fan-out runs at $10/$50 with $0.25 cache reads it mostly cannot use (each lane starts cache-cold). The vendor's own guidance points the other way twice: Opus 5 is «the model the docs tell you to start with», and on Fable 5.1 «At low … often competitive with Claude Opus and Claude Sonnet models on cost per task while scoring higher» — i.e. when Fable IS the right lane, its cheap rung is the first thing to try, and `ultracode` (which sends xhigh) is a session setting that a lane inherits unless bound. Registry-level rule (2026-09-02): bind model AND effort on every lane; T1 only for lanes whose failure cost justifies it (architecture, ambiguous requirements, final adversarial review); never let a T1 × xhigh|max lane exist by inheritance. Reference mechanism: a PreToolUse guard that reads the session model and denies unbound Agent/Workflow lanes (plugins/superscalar/reference/lane-model-guard.cjs). Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config · https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-1 2026-10-08: the vendor start-here row is Opus 5.5 (since 2026-09-22), not Opus 5; ultracode no longer sends xhigh by itself (2.1.284); and the Agent tool gained a per-invocation `effort` (2.1.292) that the reference guard does not read yet — see harnessBinding «Claude Code» and the watchlist.

Vendor-stated cross-model ordering (model-selection guide, 2026-09-30): Luna·Low < Luna·Extra high < GPT-6.1 Sol·Medium < GPT-6.1 Sol·Extra high < Astra·Low < Astra·Medium < Astra·Extra high. The vendor places the cheap rung of the bigger model ABOVE the top rung of the smaller one. That is the opposite of the Anthropic generation-bump pattern already recorded here, and it is OpenAI's claim for its own lineup, not a measurement. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/model-selection

MEASURED IN-HOUSE (Superscalar Bench, 2026-09-30 → 10-09; report: SuperscalarBench.md; each measured model's own result is on its row under inHouse) — single-observer evidence on private tasks, so weigh it as such: 6 coding tasks on a ladder of designed scope (mechanical multi-file edit → spec-complete implementation → multi-step feature with schema migration → diagnose-and-fix from a symptom report → design-and-build of a small language interpreter → crash-safe transactional key-value store), each graded by a hidden acceptance suite, every effort level, n = 3 per cell; n = 1 for Opus 4.8, Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 (further runs being measured); Fable 5.1: one cell with n = 2; 1,421 valid runs over 20 models on 4 harnesses, headless. Runs missed only on aims 5 and 6: of the 11 task × effort cells that missed at least once, 6 were the model's lowest effort and 2 ended on Claude Code's default 64K output cap (a harness limit, kept as measured) — GPT-5.6 Luna low aim 5 1/3, GPT-5.6 Terra low aim 5 2/3, GPT-5.6 Terra medium aim 5 2/3, GPT-5.6 Terra high aim 5 2/3, Gemini 3.1 Pro low aim 6 2/3, GPT-5.6 Luna low aim 6 0/3, GPT-5.6 Terra medium aim 6 2/3, GPT-6 Luna low aim 6 1/3, Haiku 4.5 default aim 6 0/3, Sonnet 5 xhigh aim 6 0/1 [cap], Sonnet 5 max aim 6 0/1 [cap]; a miss at the lowest rung is the case the escalate-on-observed-failure rule below is for. Within one model the top rung is a cost multiplier, not a quality lever on such tasks: low → max multiplied cost per verified result by 1.50×–19× (geometric mean over tasks; highest Haiku 5.5). Generations, trust cost newer ÷ older (geometric mean over tasks): Fable 5.1 vs Fable 5 low 0.70× · medium 0.55× · high 0.62× · xhigh 1.06× · max 2.41×; Opus 5.5 vs Opus 5 low 0.39× · medium 0.34× · high 0.30× · xhigh 0.60× · max 1.00×; Opus 5.5 vs Opus 4.8 low 0.40× · medium 0.35× · high 0.42× · xhigh 0.57× · max 1.00×; Sonnet 5.5 vs Sonnet 5 low 0.52× · medium 0.48× · high 0.36× · xhigh 0.89× · max 2.43×; GPT-6.1 Sol vs GPT-6 Sol low 0.73× · medium 0.64× · high 0.71× · xhigh 0.80× · max 0.77×; GPT-6.1 Sol vs GPT-5.6 Sol low 0.29× · medium 0.29× · high 0.27× · xhigh 0.35× · max 0.34×; GPT-6 Luna vs GPT-5.6 Luna low 0.35× · medium 0.33× · high 0.23× · xhigh 0.35× · max 0.26×; grok-4.7 vs grok-4.6 low 1.64× · medium 1.93× · high 1.87× · xhigh 2.03×. Practical rule: start at low/medium, escalate only on an observed failure, and treat max as an escalation of last resort rather than a default.
planGating: Claude Code — Pro: `default` resolves to Opus 5.5 since v2.1.280 («Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise, and Anthropic API: defaults to Opus 5.5»; «Before v2.1.280, `default` resolved to Sonnet 5 on Pro and Team Standard»). Opus with the 1M window "Requires usage credits" on Pro — it is included with subscription only on Max/Team/Enterprise. Sonnet 5.5 runs the 1M window in Claude Code on the Anthropic API with «no usage credits required on any plan». Sonnet 4.6 at 1M needs credits on every plan including Max.

Claude Code — Max (5x/20x) and Team Premium seats: `default` resolves to Opus 5.5 since v2.1.280 (previously Opus 5). Opus is auto-upgraded to 1M context with no configuration. Fable (5.1 since 2026-09-01 — `fable` resolves to the latest Fable, `best` to the latest Fable where available else `opus`) is never the default on any account type or provider: reach it via /model fable; it needs Claude Code ≥ v2.1.255, may bill usage credits depending on plan and seat tier (the picker shows «Requires usage credits» and interactive sessions ask consent first; Enterprise members on org billing are not prompted), and it is hidden entirely under zero data retention. Settings still pinned to the literal `claude-fable-5` are auto-rewritten to the `fable` alias on the first run of v2.1.255+.

Claude Code — Team Standard and Enterprise subscription seats: `default` resolves to Opus 5.5 since v2.1.280 — before that it resolved to Sonnet 5 on Team Standard (the seat-tier split this row used to record is gone for the default model). Seat billing tier still decides credit gating for 1M Opus and for Fable.

Claude Code — Enterprise governance: admins can disable individual models org-wide or per custom role (Haiku can never be disabled, so every member always retains one usable model), set an organization default model that replaces the account-type default, and — Enterprise only — set a MAXIMUM EFFORT LEVEL PER MODEL PER ROLE. Levels above the cap vanish from the /effort picker and --effort requests run at the cap; the clamp warns in interactive and plain --print runs but "with json or stream-json output or in background agents, the clamp applies silently." A scripted agent can therefore run below its requested effort with no signal.

Claude Code — Anthropic API key: `default` resolves to Opus 5.5 (v2.1.280+), full lineup available, `opus`→Opus 5.5 / `sonnet`→Sonnet 5.5 (v2.1.284+) / `best`→Fable 5.1 where entitled. No subscription cap; org TPM/RPM limits apply, and Opus 5 draws on a separate rate-limit bucket from the combined Opus 4.x pool. 2026-10-08: `haiku` → Haiku 5.5 on the Anthropic API from v2.1.293.

Claude Code — third-party providers are a generation behind on aliases: on Microsoft Foundry `default` resolves to Sonnet 4.5, and the `opus` alias still resolves to Opus 4.6 there. Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform resolved `default` to Sonnet 4.5 before v2.1.207. Organization effort limits are NOT delivered on Bedrock/Google Cloud/Foundry/Claude Platform on AWS — use availableModels in managed settings instead. 2026-09-29 (Claude Code model-config): the `sonnet` alias splits by provider — Anthropic API → Sonnet 5.5; Claude Platform on AWS → Sonnet 4.6; Amazon Bedrock / Google Cloud's Agent Platform / Microsoft Foundry → Sonnet 4.5. Sonnet 5.5 itself is offered on all of those platforms by id — only the alias lags. 2026-10-08: `haiku` splits the same way (Anthropic API → Haiku 5.5; Claude Platform on AWS / Bedrock / Google Cloud / Foundry → Haiku 4.5), and the `sonnet` / Foundry-`default` target claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 is Deprecated with retirement 2026-11-30.

Claude Code — subagent model resolution order (this is where a tiered-composition policy actually lands): CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL → per-invocation `model` parameter → subagent frontmatter `model` → main conversation's model. Frontmatter accepts sonnet/opus/haiku/fable, a full id, or `inherit` (the default), and a separate `effort` frontmatter field overrides the session level while that subagent runs. Note the built-in Explore agent no longer forces Haiku: as of v2.1.198 it inherits the main model, capped at Opus on the Claude API — define a project subagent named Explore with `model: haiku` to put exploration back on a cheap lane. Concurrency default is 20 subagents per session (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS), and ultracode sessions are exempt from that limit. CORRECTED 2026-10-08: the order written above is the PRE-v2.1.251 one; since v2.1.251 it is per-invocation `model` → frontmatter `model` → CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL (a default) → the main model, with CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1 (v2.1.257+) above the chain (see harnessBinding «Claude Code»). Explore is no longer «capped at Opus»: it runs on the `opus` alias target (Opus 5.5) with a subscription, Console account or LLM gateway, and stays on the main model on Bedrock / Google Cloud / Foundry / Claude Platform on AWS / Claude apps gateway. The Agent tool also takes a per-invocation `effort` since 2.1.292.

Claude Code — fast mode: Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 only, at $10/$50 per MTok for up to ~2.5x output tokens/sec. Heavily gated: an API research preview needing the fast-mode-2026-02-01 beta header plus account-manager/waitlist access; in Claude Code it requires usage credits turned on, draws from credits from the first token even when plan usage remains, needs Owner enablement on Team/Enterprise, is CLI-only (not the VS Code extension), and is unavailable on Bedrock/Google Cloud/Foundry/Claude Platform on AWS. Enable at session start — the first enable re-bills the whole context at fast-mode uncached input price. Opus 4.7 fast mode was REMOVED 2026-07-24 while Claude Code still treats 4.7 as fast-mode-capable, so /fast on 4.7 produces API rejections. 2026-10-08: Opus 5.5 has fast mode too — $8 / $40 (research preview, Claude API first-party only); Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 $10 / $50.

Codex — Plus ($20/mo): current roster (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models, 2026-09-30): gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna, gpt-6-astra (per the pricing-page usage table), gpt-5.6-sol/terra/luna («remain available during the rollout»); gpt-5.5 retires 2026-10-14. Retired from Codex with ChatGPT sign-in: gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.4-mini (2026-08-31 → gpt-6-sol / gpt-6-luna) and gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-09-14). Local messages per 5h (Plus and Standard Business): Astra 5-45 · 6.1 Sol 15-160 · 6 Sol 15-150 · Luna 350-3,000. Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing. This is the tier where Sol-on-every-lane is not viable — a wide fan-out must run Terra or Luna. 2026-10-08: the live Codex catalog already hides gpt-5.5 ahead of the 2026-10-14 retirement; ChatGPT Power presets are «Luna High, GPT-6 Sol Light, GPT-6 Sol Medium, Astra Light, Astra Medium, and Astra Extra High». Plus-plan message bands unchanged (Astra 5-45 · 6.1 Sol 15-160 · 6 Sol 15-150 · Luna 350-3,000).

Codex — Pro ($100 / $200 / $500): everything on Plus. Pro plans «currently have no five-hour limit» (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing, 2026-09-30), which replaces the earlier ~75-1,800 Sol-message bands; it is still the first tier with real headroom for many-subagent operation. Astra Ultrafast is on the $500 Pro plan only. gpt-5.3-codex-spark was retired 2026-09-14, so the earlier «everything on Plus plus codex-spark» clause is void.

Codex — Business ($25/user/mo, min 2): the same roster as Plus (Standard Business shares Plus's per-5h estimates in the current usage table, learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing, 2026-09-30), and it does not inherit Pro's 5x/20x multipliers — a Business seat has Plus-sized headroom for fan-out. A common planning error is assuming the paid-team tier buys concurrency.

Codex — Enterprise/Edu and bring-your-own-key: model availability "follows the API models available to your key"; flexible-pricing workspaces have no fixed rate limits and scale with credits. With a BYO key you "Pay only for the tokens Codex uses, based on API pricing" — the ceiling becomes org rate limits and budget rather than a 5-hour window, which is the only configuration where per-lane model choice is a pure cost question.

Codex — per-agent binding (the mechanism a tiered policy needs): agent files at ~/.codex/agents/<name>.toml or .codex/agents/<name>.toml take `model` and `model_reasoning_effort`, and "If a custom agent file sets model or model_reasoning_effort, the value in the file takes precedence." Global [agents] keys: enabled (default true), max_concurrent_threads_per_session, default_subagent_model, default_subagent_reasoning_effort. Session controls: /model, /effort, --model/-m, --reasoning-effort/-e.

Gemini CLI — maximum model requests per user per day: Gemini Code Assist (Individual) 1,000; Google AI Pro 1,500; Google AI Ultra 2,000; Code Assist Standard 1,500; Code Assist Enterprise 2,000; Gemini API key free/unpaid 250 and "Model requests to Flash model only"; paid API key and Vertex "Varies". Two things matter for agent design: one prompt can be dozens of model requests, and model availability is "across the Gemini model family as determined by Gemini CLI" — per-model selection is not plan-gated, the CLI chooses.

Gemini CLI — model selection lags the API materially. The CLI's valid-model set does not include gemini-3.6-flash or gemini-3.5-flash-lite, still hardcodes gemini-2.5-pro as DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL (a model with an announced 2026-10-16 shutdown) and gemini-3-pro-preview in its picker (shut down 2026-03-09). Selection surfaces: --model/-m (highest precedence) → GEMINI_MODEL → project settings → user settings; per-subagent via agents.overrides.<agentName>.modelConfig.model, since /model "does not override the model used by sub-agents". harnessBinding.perLaneModel: Agent tool per-invocation `model`; subagent frontmatter `model` (sonnet|opus|haiku|fable | full id | `inherit`, the default); `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` env default; `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` (v2.1.257+) to override every definition. Resolution order (v2.1.251+): per-invocation `model` → definition frontmatter `model` (where `inherit` = the main conversation) → `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` → the main conversation's model. NOTE THE REVERSAL: before v2.1.251 the env var came FIRST and overrode both the per-invocation parameter and the frontmatter — this registry carried that older order until 2026-09-05, so any lane logic written against it had the priority inverted. Setting the env var to `inherit` is the same as leaving it unset. 2026-10-08 re-read (raw sub-agents.md): order unchanged. FORCE scope: «To apply one model to every subagent, teammate, and workflow agent, also set `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE` to `1`.» — it voids Workflow agent() opts.model too. «Setting CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL by itself doesn't change the model the built-in Explore and Plan subagents run on.» «An alias in `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` always resolves to the version the alias points to, even when it names the main conversation's family.» Alias table (model-config.md): Anthropic API opus / sonnet / haiku = Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 (`haiku` from v2.1.293); Claude Platform on AWS = Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 4.6 / Haiku 4.5; Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform = Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 4.5 / Haiku 4.5; Microsoft Foundry = Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.5 / Haiku 4.5. Default model: Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise and Anthropic API → Opus 5.5; Claude Platform on AWS / Bedrock / Google Cloud → Opus 5.5; Foundry → Sonnet 4.5. Managed allowlist (2.1.283): `availableModelsMatch: "exact"` («an `availableModels` entry allows only the model version it names, so new releases stay blocked until listed» — e.g. Haiku 5.5 behind `haiku`) and `deniedModels` (blocks a model even when availableModels allows it).
harnessBinding.perLaneEffort: subagent and skill frontmatter `effort` (low|medium|high|xhigh|max, available levels per model) — overrides the session level while that subagent or skill runs, but NOT the environment variable; session-level `--effort` at launch · `/effort` · `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`. There is no per-subagent *thinking* setting: since v2.1.198 a subagent inherits the main conversation's extended-thinking configuration. VERIFY, don't assume: `/tasks` names the model each running subagent is on and adds the effort level when the subagent definition or the skill it forked from sets `effort` (v2.1.242+) — that is the cheapest check that a lane binding actually applied. `/effort s` (v2.1.257+) scopes an effort change to the current session only, matching `/model`. 2026-10-08: Claude Code 2.1.292 (2026-10-06) «Added an `effort` parameter to the Agent tool, so Claude runs a sub-agent at the effort level you ask for» — a per-invocation effort knob now exists. The sub-agents reference page does NOT document it yet (its only effort mentions are the frontmatter row and the /tasks note), so its precedence vs frontmatter `effort`, the session level and CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL is UNVERIFIED — do not assume the frontmatter rule («Overrides the session effort level, but not the CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL environment variable») governs it. The CLI installed here is 2.1.284 and cannot exercise it. Lane effort knobs now: Agent `effort` (≥ 2.1.292), frontmatter `effort`, Workflow agent() opts.effort.

caveats: Default effort (model-config.md, verbatim 2026-10-08): «`high` on every model that supports effort, except that Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5 default to `medium`, Opus 4.7 defaults to `xhigh`, and, when your organization sets a default effort level for its organization default model, that level is the default when you run that model.» A top-level `effortLevel` in the USER settings file does not apply to Opus 5.5; project, local, managed or --settings `effortLevel` applies to every model. (Until 2026-10-08 this caveat read «high on every effort-capable model except Opus 4.7 (xhigh)».)

Fable 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 hold a first-run default-effort choice across sessions; the vendor states Opus 5 and Fable 5.1 have no such hold. Since v2.1.257 `--effort` lifts a held model's hold for that session only rather than permanently, and an effort picked on claude.ai for a Remote Control session applies during the hold.

`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` is a DEFAULT, not a pin — a definition's `model` or a model Claude passes per invocation both beat it (v2.1.251+). Only `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` (v2.1.257+) makes it win, and while FORCE is on Claude Code ignores every definition's `model` field including the built-in Explore and Plan agents and Claude cannot pass a model at spawn; setting FORCE alone (no model) puts every subagent on the main conversation's model. Two lanes escape FORCE anyway: a conversation fork, and a skill run in a subagent with `model: inherit`. Blocked-by-allowlist values no longer fall through silently in every case: since v2.1.222 a blocked FAMILY alias runs on the newest permitted version of that family, other blocked values fall back to the inherited model, and interactive sessions print a warning naming both models — headless/scripted lanes are where the substitution is still unannounced. 2026-10-08 exception: «If you set only `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE`, subagents run on the main conversation's model, except that the built-in Explore subagent runs on the model listed for it under Built-in subagents.» With both variables set, every subagent runs on CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL.

The built-in Explore agent inherits the main conversation's model (since v2.1.198, no longer forced to Haiku) but ON THE CLAUDE API IT IS CAPPED AT OPUS — a Fable-5.1 main session runs Explore on Opus 5, not on Fable, and a Sonnet or Haiku session runs Explore on that same model. On Bedrock / Google Cloud / Microsoft Foundry / Claude Platform on AWS there is no cap and Explore inherits directly. To put exploration on a cheap lane, define a user or project subagent named `Explore` with `model: haiku` — it overrides the built-in and keeps its own `model` field. Plan inherits with no cap; statusline-setup is fixed to Sonnet and claude-code-guide to Haiku. RE-READ 2026-10-08 — no longer described as a cap: with a Fable main, «With a Claude subscription, an Anthropic Console account, or an LLM gateway reached through `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, Explore runs on the Opus model that the `opus` alias resolves to» (now Opus 5.5); «On Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS, or a Claude apps gateway, Explore stays on the main conversation's model.» 2.1.284: Explore inherits a model id Claude Code does not recognize (a custom model behind a proxy) instead of switching to Opus. statusline-setup = Sonnet and claude-code-guide = Haiku (which now means Haiku 5.5 on the Anthropic API) unchanged.

Enterprise admins can cap maximum effort per model per role; with json/stream-json output or in background agents the clamp applies SILENTLY, so a scripted lane can run below its requested effort with no signal.

Frontmatter `model:` on custom commands and skills was IGNORED in interactive sessions until 2.1.259 fixed it — a lane binding written as command/skill frontmatter and «verified» on a build before 2.1.259 was never actually exercised. The same release also stopped auto mode from running a turn on a model it does not support when frontmatter named one (it now keeps the session model). Re-verify any guard that assumes frontmatter enforcement against a build ≥ 2.1.259.

2.1.261 added `--append-subagent-system-prompt-file` (read the subagent system prompt from a file, for prompts too large for the command line) — a per-lane configuration surface that does not appear in perLaneModel/perLaneEffort and is invisible to any guard that only inspects the invocation's `model`/`effort` arguments. 2.1.261 also added `bashOutputMaxChars` / `taskOutputMaxChars` (up to 128K inline before spooling to a file), which changes how much a fan-out lane's output costs the parent, and 2.1.260 removed the one-hour time limit on background commands started by subagents.

ultracode cannot be set through `effortLevel` or `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`, and an env level other than `xhigh` leaves ultracode's workflow orchestration inactive with no signal — a scripted ultracode lane can run as plain effort. STALE since v2.1.284 (inside the previous pass's window): «Changed Ultracode into its own toggle in `/effort` (Tab, or `/effort ultracode [on|off]`): it no longer forces xhigh effort and stays on at any effort level»; «If `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` or an effort cap sets the session's level, ultracode stays on at that level.» There is a persistent `"ultracode": true` settings key (also --settings or an SDK control request); only `--effort ultracode` / SDK effortLevel 'ultracode' also set xhigh. So an env level no longer disables orchestration silently — and a session can be ultracode at medium, which an «ultracode = xhigh | max» heuristic (the reference guard's) misses.

Before v2.1.260, `model: fable` subagents ignored the `[1m]` tag on an `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL` pin and ran at 200K silently, and Fable 5.1 prompt caching did not cover context attached after tool results — both are pre-2.1.260 correctness and billing faults, not model behavior.

ultracode is a SESSION setting, not a lane setting: the Agent tool has no per-invocation effort, so a Fable lane under an ultracode session inherits xhigh unless its definition sets `effort`; Workflow `agent()` opts.effort is the per-lane knob. Verify with `/tasks` (v2.1.242+), which names each running subagent's model and its effort when the definition or skill set one — assert observed behavior, not requested settings. STALE 2026-10-08 on two counts: the Agent tool HAS a per-invocation `effort` since 2.1.292 (precedence undocumented), and since 2.1.284 an ultracode session no longer implies xhigh, so the inherited level is whatever the session runs at.

CONTENT-BASED AUTOMATIC MODEL FALLBACK CAN CHANGE YOUR TIER WITHOUT ASKING, and it is directly relevant to security-adjacent repos. Fable 5: biology-flagged → re-runs on Opus 5; cybersecurity-flagged → Opus 4.8. Opus 5: cybersecurity-flagged → Opus 4.8; biology-flagged → refusal with no fallback. A flagged request can trip on the FIRST request from CLAUDE.md content or git status alone, and after fallback the session STAYS on the fallback model. If availableModels blocks the fallback target, no fallback happens and the request simply refuses. Requires v2.1.219+; `claude --safe-mode` isolates whether local customizations are the trigger. 2026-09-02: the same routing applies to Fable 5.1 (biology → Opus 5, cybersecurity → Opus 4.8, per the Claude Code model-config page); the API-side equivalent is fallbacks:"default" (beta), whose permitted targets for 5.1 are Opus 4.8 and Opus 5. 2026-10-08: (1) the Fable 5.1 / Fable 5 / Opus 5.5 → biology Opus 5, cyber Opus 4.8; Opus 5 → cyber Opus 4.8, biology refusal; Sonnet 5.5 → cyber Sonnet 5, biology refusal routing is unchanged; since 2.1.287 a switch keeps the session's effort. (2) claude-haiku-5-5 has NO fallback at all. (3) API fallbacks are visible (response `model`, `fallback` block, `fallback_message` in usage.iterations) — the hidden case is sticky routing. (4) Refusals before any output are billed again since 2026-09-24 for categories bio, frontier_llm and reasoning_extraction («charged like any other request, at the rates of the model that ran it»); cyber and general_harms stay free.
